task.prompt:
You are analyzing a voltage-controlled ring oscillator in SPICE.
The circuit below is FULLY SPECIFIED - every parameter already has a
fixed value. Predict its performance WITHOUT running a simulator, using
circuit analysis (gm/ID, pole-zero reasoning, etc).

Netlist (all values fixed):
.options gmin=1e-12 reltol=1e-4 abstol=1e-13 vntol=1e-7 itl1=500 noacct
.model NMOS NMOS (LEVEL=1 VTO=0.7 KP=110u GAMMA=0.4 LAMBDA=0.04
+ TOX=20n PHI=0.7 CGSO=0.4n CGDO=0.4n CJ=0.4m CJSW=0.8n MJ=0.5)
.model PMOS PMOS (LEVEL=1 VTO=-0.7 KP=50u GAMMA=0.57 LAMBDA=0.05
+ TOX=20n PHI=0.8 CGSO=0.4n CGDO=0.4n CJ=0.4m CJSW=0.8n MJ=0.5)
Vdd vdd 0 3.3
Vctrl ctrl cx 2.500000e+00
Vdelta cx 0 0
.ic v(n1)=0 v(n2)=3.3 v(n3)=0
Mp1 n1 n3 vdd vdd PMOS W=6.180083e-05 L=1.203075e-06
Mn1 n1 n3 s1 0 NMOS W=3.476043e-05 L=1.203075e-06
Ms1 s1 ctrl 0 0 NMOS W=1.265910e-05 L=1.203075e-06
C1 n1 0 1.437007e-13
Mp2 n2 n1 vdd vdd PMOS W=6.180083e-05 L=1.203075e-06
Mn2 n2 n1 s2 0 NMOS W=3.476043e-05 L=1.203075e-06
Ms2 s2 ctrl 0 0 NMOS W=1.265910e-05 L=1.203075e-06
C2 n2 0 1.437007e-13
Mp3 n3 n2 vdd vdd PMOS W=6.180083e-05 L=1.203075e-06
Mn3 n3 n2 s3 0 NMOS W=3.476043e-05 L=1.203075e-06
Ms3 s3 ctrl 0 0 NMOS W=1.265910e-05 L=1.203075e-06
C3 n3 0 1.437007e-13

Measurement definitions (in order):
Transient sampling step and duration 0.5n 500n uic
ta (tran) = WHEN v(n1)=1.65 RISE=3
tb (tran) = WHEN v(n1)=1.65 RISE=8
f0 = 5/(tb-ta)
pwr = 3.3*mean(abs(i(Vdd)))
For subsequent measurements change Vdelta = 0.2
Transient sampling step and duration 0.5n 500n uic
tc (tran) = WHEN v(n1)=1.65 RISE=3
td (tran) = WHEN v(n1)=1.65 RISE=8
f1 = 5/(td-tc)
For subsequent measurements change Vdelta = 0
For subsequent measurements change Vdd = 3.5
Transient sampling step and duration 0.5n 500n uic
te (tran) = WHEN v(n1)=1.65 RISE=3
tf (tran) = WHEN v(n1)=1.65 RISE=8
f2 = 5/(tf-te)
power_w = pwr.
fosc_hz = f0. kvco = (f1 - f0)/0.2. pushing = abs(f2 - f0)/0.2.



Predict these characteristics, in plain SI units (no dB where the
unit says otherwise, no mW where the unit says W):
  fosc_hz  - Oscillation freq, Hz
  kvco     - Tuning gain, Hz/V
  pushing  - Supply pushing, Hz/V
  power_w  - Total power, W

Work analytically. Do not run, invoke, or ask another tool to run any
circuit simulator (including SPICE, ngspice, or LTspice).
Keep the explanation concise: aim for 2–4 short calculation steps. State the
key physical assumption, substitute the circuit values into the relevant equations,
and give the essential intermediate numerical results with units. Group related
metrics in one step. Write each calculation inline as plain text on one line,
with the formula, substitution, result and unit together. Use * for multiplication,
/ for division and ^ for powers. Avoid LaTeX, display math and stacked fractions.
End with a JSON object containing
the same final numbers in the requested units using these keys:
{"fosc_hz": <float>, "kvco": <float>, "pushing": <float>, "power_w": <float>}

task.netlist:
* three-stage current-starved ring oscillator
.options gmin=1e-12 reltol=1e-4 abstol=1e-13 vntol=1e-7 itl1=500 noacct

.model NMOS NMOS (LEVEL=1 VTO=0.7 KP=110u GAMMA=0.4 LAMBDA=0.04
+ TOX=20n PHI=0.7 CGSO=0.4n CGDO=0.4n CJ=0.4m CJSW=0.8n MJ=0.5)
.model PMOS PMOS (LEVEL=1 VTO=-0.7 KP=50u GAMMA=0.57 LAMBDA=0.05
+ TOX=20n PHI=0.8 CGSO=0.4n CGDO=0.4n CJ=0.4m CJSW=0.8n MJ=0.5)

Vdd vdd 0 3.3
* the control voltage is split in two so the sweep step can be applied by
* altering a source instead of evaluating arithmetic in the netlist
Vctrl ctrl cx 2.500000e+00
Vdelta cx 0 0

* a ring has no stable dc solution to start from - the initial condition
* kicks it and every run is done with uic
.ic v(n1)=0 v(n2)=3.3 v(n3)=0

* --- stage 1: inverter whose ground return is starved by Ms1 ---
Mp1 n1 n3 vdd vdd PMOS W=6.180083e-05 L=1.203075e-06
Mn1 n1 n3 s1 0 NMOS W=3.476043e-05 L=1.203075e-06
Ms1 s1 ctrl 0 0 NMOS W=1.265910e-05 L=1.203075e-06
C1 n1 0 1.437007e-13
* --- stage 2 ---
Mp2 n2 n1 vdd vdd PMOS W=6.180083e-05 L=1.203075e-06
Mn2 n2 n1 s2 0 NMOS W=3.476043e-05 L=1.203075e-06
Ms2 s2 ctrl 0 0 NMOS W=1.265910e-05 L=1.203075e-06
C2 n2 0 1.437007e-13
* --- stage 3 ---
Mp3 n3 n2 vdd vdd PMOS W=6.180083e-05 L=1.203075e-06
Mn3 n3 n2 s3 0 NMOS W=3.476043e-05 L=1.203075e-06
Ms3 s3 ctrl 0 0 NMOS W=1.265910e-05 L=1.203075e-06
C3 n3 0 1.437007e-13

.control
set noaskquit

* --- run 1: nominal control voltage and nominal supply ---
tran 0.5n 500n uic
meas tran ta WHEN v(n1)=1.65 RISE=3
meas tran tb WHEN v(n1)=1.65 RISE=8
let f0 = 5/(tb-ta)
let pwr = 3.3*mean(abs(i(Vdd)))
* each run opens a new plot, so every result is written out before the
* next tran starts - scalars do not survive a plot change
echo "$&f0 $&pwr" > f0.txt

* --- run 2: control voltage stepped by +200 mV -> tuning gain ---
alter Vdelta = 0.2
tran 0.5n 500n uic
meas tran tc WHEN v(n1)=1.65 RISE=3
meas tran td WHEN v(n1)=1.65 RISE=8
let f1 = 5/(td-tc)
echo "$&f1" > f1.txt

* --- run 3: control restored, supply stepped by +200 mV -> pushing ---
alter Vdelta = 0
alter Vdd = 3.5
tran 0.5n 500n uic
meas tran te WHEN v(n1)=1.65 RISE=3
meas tran tf WHEN v(n1)=1.65 RISE=8
let f2 = 5/(tf-te)
echo "$&f2" > f2.txt
quit
.endc
.end

explanation_steps: Estimate: A three-stage ring needs six stage delays per period. At load Cl = 1.4370071096111147e-13 F the nominal charge for a rail-to-rail transition is Cl × VDD = 1.4370071096111147e-13 × 3.3 = 4.742123e-13 C.

Simulate env/circuits/vco.sp (ac91325bffdd) with ngspice -b after substituting SI parameters {"Wp": 6.180083024992617e-05, "Wn": 3.476042641450456e-05, "Ws": 1.2659104738727196e-05, "L": 1.203075038293806e-06, "Cl": 1.4370071096111147e-13, "Vc": 2.5}. Count five periods at nominal bias, then repeat with control and supply each raised separately by 0.2 V. Power = 3.3 × mean(|I(Vdd)|) at nominal bias.

From measured values (rounded): Five periods span the third through eighth rising edges: f ≈ 5/(1.65336E-08 - 4.86309E-09) Hz. Control sensitivity = (4.62617E+08 - 4.2843E+08)/0.2 = 1.70935e+08 Hz/V; supply sensitivity = abs(4.45763E+08 - 4.2843E+08)/0.2 = 8.6665e+07 Hz/V.

baseline_results.chatgpt_answer:
Key assumption: The three-stage ring is dominated by the explicit 143.7007 fF load per stage. The NMOS starving transistor limits the falling-edge current, while the PMOS provides a faster rising edge. Use LEVEL=1 square-law MOS equations and approximate propagation delays.

1. Device parameters and discharge current

NMOS starving-device ratio: W/L = 12.65910/1.203075 = 10.5223.

Starving-device transconductance parameter: beta_s = 110e-6 * 10.5223 = 0.00115745 A/V^2.

Nominal overdrive: Vov = 2.5 - 0.7 = 1.8 V.

The ideal saturation-current ceiling is Isat = 0.5 * 0.00115745 * 1.8^2 = 0.001875 A.

Accounting approximately for the series NMOS, source degeneration, and finite output voltage, use an effective falling-edge current of 0.00125 A.

2. Oscillation frequency

Approximate rising-edge current from the PMOS strength and output swing as 0.0020 A.

Falling delay: tfall = 143.7007e-15 * 1.65 / 0.00125 = 1.897e-10 s.

Rising delay: trise = 143.7007e-15 * 1.65 / 0.0020 = 1.186e-10 s.

Oscillation period: T = 3 * (1.897e-10 + 1.186e-10) = 9.249e-10 s.

Oscillation frequency: fosc_hz = 1 / 9.249e-10 = 1.0812e9 Hz.

3. Tuning gain and supply pushing

At Vctrl = 2.7 V, the ideal starving-device saturation-current ceiling increases by (2.7 - 0.7)^2 / (2.5 - 0.7)^2 = 1.23457.

Allowing for series-device limitations, estimate an effective discharge-current increase of approximately 14%, giving f1 ≈ 1.146e9 Hz.

Tuning gain: kvco = (1.146e9 - 1.0812e9) / 0.2 = 3.24e8 Hz/V.

For Vdd = 3.5 V, assume increased switching swing partially offsets the stronger PMOS drive, giving f2 ≈ 1.102e9 Hz.

Supply pushing: pushing = abs(1.102e9 - 1.0812e9) / 0.2 = 1.04e8 Hz/V.

4. Total supply power

Assume approximately one full 143.7007 fF capacitive charging event per stage per oscillation period, plus a small short-circuit contribution.

Capacitive power: Pcap = 3 * 143.7007e-15 * 3.3^2 * 1.0812e9 = 0.005073 W.

Including approximately 8% additional switching current: power_w = 0.005073 * 1.08 = 0.005479 W.

These are analytical estimates, not simulator-verified values. In particular, the effective switching currents and supply-pushing estimate are approximate.

Final predictions
fosc_hz	1.0812e9 Hz
kvco	3.24e8 Hz/V
pushing	1.04e8 Hz/V
power_w	0.005479 W

baseline_results.claude_answer:
**Assumption:** this is a 3-stage current-starved ring oscillator. The starved NMOS sets the discharge current, and the PMOS pull-up is much stronger. The estimate is a hand calculation with no simulator run.

1. **Discharge current.**
   - Starve device: W/L = 12.66u/1.203u = 10.5, beta_s = 110u*10.5 = 1.16 mA/V^2, Vov = 2.5 - 0.7 = 1.8 V.
   - Series Mn: W/L = 28.9, beta_n = 3.18 mA/V^2, with body effect Vt ≈ 0.93 V.
   - Balancing the triode starve device against Mn gives Vds,s ≈ 1.3 V and I_disch ≈ 1.16m*(1.8*1.33 - 1.33^2/2) ≈ 1.7 mA.
   - The PMOS has beta_p = 2.57 mA/V^2 and Vov = 2.6 V, so it can supply about 5-8 mA when it conducts.

2. **Load and frequency.**
   - C_load ≈ 144 fF (explicit) + 134 fF (next-stage gate, 2/3*Cox*W*L) + about 100 fF (overlap with Miller effect, junctions) ≈ 0.38 pF.
   - Fall delay ≈ C*1.65/I ≈ 0.38p*1.65/1.75m ≈ 0.36 ns.
   - Rise delay ≈ 0.38p*1.65/5m ≈ 0.13 ns.
   - fosc ≈ 1/(3*(0.36n + 0.13n)) ≈ 1/1.47n ≈ 6.8e8 Hz, which I round down to 6.5e8 Hz for finite input slew.

3. **Tuning gain and supply pushing.**
   - A +0.2 V step raises Vov to 2.0 V, so the starve current rises about 15-18%.
   - That raises f by about 12%, from 650 to 730 MHz, so kvco ≈ 80 MHz/0.2 V ≈ 4.0e8 Hz/V.
   - Raising Vdd to 3.5 V increases the Mn1 gate drive and current by about 4%, but the swing and trip-point delay grow by about 6%. These nearly cancel, leaving a shift of about +6 MHz, so pushing ≈ 3e7 Hz/V.

4. **Power.**
   - Charge per cycle is about C*Vdd per stage, so I_avg ≈ 3*0.35p*3.3*6.5e8 ≈ 2.25 mA, plus about 10% crowbar current ≈ 2.5 mA.
   - P ≈ 3.3 V * 2.5 mA ≈ 8.2e-3 W.

{"fosc_hz": 6.5e8, "kvco": 4.0e8, "pushing": 3.0e7, "power_w": 8.2e-3}

**Key assumption:** this is a 3-stage current-starved ring. The PMOS pull-up is strong and the NMOS pull-down is limited by the starve device Ms. Output rises are fast and falls are slow, so the period is about 3*(t_fall + t_rise).

**1. Starve current and node capacitance**
- Ms overdrive: Vov_s = Vctrl - VTO = 1.4538 - 0.7 = 0.754 V, with W/L = 16.38u/3.506u = 4.67.
- Ms saturation current: Id ≈ 0.5*110u*4.67*0.754^2 ≈ 146 uA, which is about 153 uA with channel-length modulation.
- Mn (W/L = 2.05) alone could carry about 0.5*110u*2.05*(3.3-1.25-0.92)^2 ≈ 155 uA at Vs ≈ 1.25 V, so Ms sets the discharge current of about 150 uA.
- PMOS saturation current: 0.5*50u*8.36*(3.3-0.7)^2 ≈ 1.4 mA, roughly 9x stronger than the pull-down.
- Node capacitance: C = 514 fF explicit + about 170 fF of gate and overlap load (Cox = 1.73 mF/m^2, so Cg(Mn+Mp) ≈ 221 fF at full gate cap) + about 15 fF of own overlap ≈ 0.70 pF. The netlist has no AD/PD, so there is no junction capacitance.

**2. Frequency**
- The strong PMOS pulls the inverter trip point up to about 2.0 V.
- Fall time: t_fall ≈ C*(3.3-2.0)/I_avg = 0.70p*1.3/130u ≈ 7 ns, with some extra from the PMOS still fighting at the start.
- Rise time: the PMOS sees the slowly falling input (about 0.2 V/ns). Charging 0.70p*2.0 V ≈ 1.4 pC against a ramping current gives t_rise ≈ 5 ns.
- fosc ≈ 1/(3*(7.5n+5n)) ≈ 1/37.5n ≈ 2.7e7 Hz.

**3. Tuning gain and supply pushing**
- Raising Vctrl by 0.2 V gives Vov_s = 0.954 V, so Id ≈ 0.5*110u*4.67*0.954^2*(1.04) ≈ 245 uA at Vs ≈ 1.0 V. That is about 1.6x the base current.
- Both delays scale roughly with 1/I (the rise time less so), so f1 ≈ 1.5*f0 ≈ 4.1e7 Hz.
- kvco = (f1 - f0)/0.2 = (4.1e7 - 2.7e7)/0.2 ≈ 7.0e7 Hz/V.
- Raising Vdd from 3.3 to 3.5 V barely changes the Ms current (only through lambda, about 0.3%). The voltage swing to the trip point grows by about 6% (about 1.3 V to 1.38 V), so the period lengthens slightly and f drops by about 3%.
- pushing = |Δf|/0.2 ≈ 0.8e6/0.2 ≈ 4e6 Hz/V.

**4. Power**
- Charge drawn from Vdd per stage per cycle: C*Vdd = 0.70p*3.3 ≈ 2.3 pC, plus about 0.2 pC of short-circuit charge through the overlapping PMOS and Mn conduction.
- Idd ≈ 3 stages*2.5p*2.7e7 ≈ 2.0e-4 A.
- P = 3.3*Idd ≈ 6.7e-4 W.

**Assumption:** this is a 3-stage current-starved ring. The PMOS is strong and unrestricted (W/L = 64), so rising edges are fast. The falling edge is limited by the NMOS stack of Mn in series with the Ms current source, so the fall slew rate sets the frequency.

**Step 1 – Starved current and node capacitance**
- Ms: W/L = 6.5e-6/0.92e-6 = 7.06, Vov = 2.245 - 0.7 = 1.545 V.
- Ms saturated: Id = 0.5*110u*7.06*1.545^2 = 0.93 mA.
- Mn is much wider (W/L = 16.8) and Vgs = 3.3 - Vs. Balancing Mn against Ms gives Vs ≈ 1.35 V and I ≈ 0.92 mA, so the stack is current-limited by Ms.
- Cox = 3.45e-11/20n = 1.73 mF/m^2. Next-stage gate channel capacitance ≈ 0.67*(1.73m*(58.9u+15.4u)*0.92u) = 79 fF.
- Overlap capacitance: gate-source 0.4n*(58.9u+15.4u) = 30 fF, Miller gate-drain 2*30 = 60 fF, own gate-drain 30 fF.
- Junction capacitance is zero because AD, AS, PD and PS default to 0.
- Ctotal = 46.4 fF + 79 fF + 30 fF + 60 fF + 30 fF ≈ 245 fF per node.

**Step 2 – Frequency**
- The inverter threshold is Vm ≈ 2.05 V, found by setting the PMOS current 1.6m*(2.6 - Vin)^2 equal to the starved NMOS current.
- Fall delay: t_f ≈ C*(3.3 - 2.05)/I_avg = 245f*1.25/0.85m ≈ 0.35 ns.
- Rise delay: the PMOS charges the node while the input falls at about 3.8 V/ns, so t_r ≈ 0.25 ns.
- T = 3*(t_f + t_r) = 3*0.60 ns = 1.8 ns, so f0 ≈ 5.6e8 Hz (taken as about 5.8e8 Hz).

**Step 3 – Power**
- Each node is charged once per cycle from Vdd, so P = 3*C*Vdd^2*f0 = 3*245f*10.89*5.8e8 ≈ 4.6 mW.
- Cross-check: three NMOS stacks each conduct ≈ 0.9 mA for about half the cycle, which gives Iavg ≈ 1.35 mA and 4.5 mW.
- I take P ≈ 4.5 mW.

**Step 4 – Tuning gain and pushing**
- Vctrl rises by 0.2 V, so Vov goes from 1.545 V to 1.745 V and the Ms current scales with Vov^2. The Mn series device compresses this, and the stack current rises from 0.92 mA to about 1.10 mA (+19%).
- Delay is roughly proportional to 1/I, so f1 ≈ 5.8e8*1.17 ≈ 6.8e8 Hz.
- kvco = (6.8e8 - 5.8e8)/0.2 ≈ 5.0e8 Hz/V.
- Vdd from 3.3 V to 3.5 V barely changes the stack current, because Ms is nearly saturated and sets it (about +1.5%). The swing grows about 6% and Vm shifts up by about 0.1 V.
- The delay rises slightly, so f2 ≈ 5.8e8*0.97 ≈ 5.64e8 Hz.
- pushing = |5.64e8 - 5.8e8|/0.2 ≈ 8e7 Hz/V.

baseline_results.claude_answer:
Assumption: this is a current-starved ring with an unstarved PMOS (W/L = 172) and a weak NMOS stack (Mn W/L = 4.2 in series with Ms W/L = 32.6). The falling edge is slow and set by the stack current. The rising edge is set by the previous stage's slow falling edge.

**Step 1: Stack current and load.**
- Ms: beta_s = 110u*32.6 = 3.58 mA/V^2, Vov_s = 1.7048 - 0.7 = 1.0048 V, so Ms is in triode.
- Mn: beta_n = 110u*4.2 = 0.462 mA/V^2, Vgs = 3.3 - Vs, with a small body effect.
- Equating Is (triode) with In (saturation) gives Vs ≈ 0.37 V and I ≈ 1.08 mA, or about 1.05 mA averaged over the discharge.
- Load: C = 1.96 pF + gate and overlap caps of the next PMOS (about 0.3 pF, no junction caps since AD = 0) ≈ 2.3 pF.
- Inverter trip point: PMOS beta = 50u*172 = 8.6 mA/V^2, so 65.6*(2.6 - Vm) = 15.2*(Vm - 0.95) gives Vm ≈ 2.3 V.

**Step 2: Frequency.**
- Fall delay: 2.3p*(3.3 - 2.3)/1.05m ≈ 2.2 ns, plus about 0.4 ns of overlap with the input edge, so about 2.6 ns.
- Rise delay: the input falls at I/C = 1.05m/2.3p ≈ 0.45 V/ns. The PMOS needs about 5 to 7 pC to push the node to Vm, so the output crosses Vm when the input is near 1.3 V. That is about 2.4 ns after the input crossed Vm.
- Period: T = 3*(2.6 + 2.4) ns = 15 ns, so fosc = 1/15n ≈ 6.7e7 Hz. I take 7.0e7 Hz.

**Step 3: Tuning gain and supply pushing.**
- Kvco: at fixed Vdd, dVs/dVctrl = -beta_s*Vs/(beta_s*(Vov - Vs) + gm_n) = -1.31m/(2.3m + 1.1m) = -0.385. Then dI/dVctrl = gm_n*0.385 ≈ 0.42 mA/V, about 39 %/V. With f ∝ I, kvco ≈ 0.39*7e7 ≈ 2.7e7 Hz/V.
- Pushing: Mn's gate is tied to Vdd, so dI/dVdd ≈ (gm_n + lambda*I)*2.3/(3.4) ≈ 0.7 mA/V, about 65 %/V. The trip point rises with Vdd (dVm/dVdd ≈ 0.8), so the swing grows by about 4 % over 0.2 V. Net df/dVdd ≈ +0.45*7e7 ≈ 3.1e7 Hz/V.

**Step 4: Power.**
- Charge per stage per cycle ≈ C*Vdd + short-circuit charge = 2.3p*3.3 + about 2 pC ≈ 10 pC.
- Idd = 3*10 pC*7e7 Hz ≈ 2.1 mA.
- pwr = 3.3*2.1 mA ≈ 6.9 mW.

ENDI estimate the oscillator as a 3-stage current-starved ring in which the Ms devices set the discharge current. All numbers are hand estimates.

**Step 1 – Starving current and node capacitance.**
- Ms has W/L = 2.273u/0.8455u = 2.69 and Vov = 2.5 - 0.7 = 1.8 V.
- Ms saturation current: Id = 0.5*110u*2.69*1.8^2*(1+0.04*Vds) = 0.48 mA*(1+0.04*Vds), about 0.53 mA at Vds ≈ 2.5 V.
- The series Mn (beta = 2.7 mA/V^2) is about 10x stronger than Ms, so Ms limits the pull-down current.
- The PMOS is strong: 0.5*50u*25.8*2.6^2 = 4.3 mA. Rising edges are therefore fast and falling edges are slow.
- Node load: C = 440 fF + gate (Cox = 1.73 mF/m^2 * 36.2 um^2 = 62 fF, ≈ 50 fF effective) + Miller and overlap (≈ 50 fF) ≈ 560 fF. The junction caps are zero because AD and PS are not specified.

**Step 2 – Frequency.**
- The trip point is where the PMOS current equals the Ms-limited current: 0.5*1.29m*Vov^2 = 0.53 mA gives Vsg ≈ 1.6 V, so the trip is at Vin ≈ 1.7 V.
- Fall delay: t_fall = C*dV/I = 560f*1.6/0.53m ≈ 1.7 ns.
- Rise delay, from about 0.4 V up to the trip: t_rise ≈ 0.5 ns.
- Period T = 3*(1.7 + 0.5) ns ≈ 6.6 ns, so fosc = 1/6.6n ≈ 1.5e8 Hz.

**Step 3 – Power and Kvco.**
- Charge per cycle: 3 nodes * 560f * ~3.0 V = 5.0 pC. At 1.5e8 Hz this gives an average current of 0.76 mA, plus about 0.07 mA of shoot-through, so Iavg ≈ 0.83 mA.
- power_w = 3.3 * 0.83 mA ≈ 2.8e-3 W.
- With Vdelta = 0.2 V, ctrl = 2.7 V and Vov = 2.0 V, so Ms current scales by (2.0/1.8)^2 = 1.23. The fall time dominates the period (and Ms drifts toward triode), so f1 ≈ 1.5e8*1.19 ≈ 1.79e8 Hz.

**Step 4 – Pushing.**
- Raising Vdd to 3.5 V moves the trip point up by almost the same amount (Vin ≈ Vdd - 1.6 V), so the fall swing to the trip stays at about 1.6 V.
- The only first-order effects are channel-length modulation of Ms (about +1% current), a slightly faster PMOS rise, and a bit more Miller charge. Together these raise f by about 1.5%.

Assumption: this is a 3-stage current-starved ring. The PMOS pull-up is un-starved, so the falling edge, limited by the series NMOS pair, sets the period. This is a hand estimate and not a simulation.

**Step 1: starved-NMOS current at Vctrl = 2.054 V**
- Ms W/L = 10.48u/0.653u = 16.06, so beta_s = 110u*16.06 = 1.77 mA/V^2 and Vov_s = 2.054 - 0.7 = 1.354 V.
- Mn W/L = 19.6, so beta_n = 2.16 mA/V^2.
- With Mn gate at 3.3 V and body effect, matching the Ms and Mn currents gives Vs ≈ 1.17 V and Id ≈ 1.6 mA.
- At Vin ≈ 2 V (near the trip point) the same matching gives only about 0.8 mA.
- The PMOS has W/L = 98.6 and beta_p = 4.9 mA/V^2, so it can deliver more than 10 mA. The inverter trip point is therefore high, Vm ≈ 2.05 V.

**Step 2: load capacitance and frequency**
- Cox = 3.45e-11/20n = 1.73 mF/m^2. Gate channel plus overlap caps of the next stage, with Miller effect, add roughly 0.19 pF.
- The junction caps are zero because AD and PS are not given.
- C_tot ≈ 0.332 pF + 0.19 pF ≈ 0.5 pF per node.
- Falling edge (3.3 to 2.05 V, net current about 1.2 mA): t_f ≈ 0.5p*1.25/1.2m ≈ 0.5 ns.
- Rising edge (0 to 2.05 V, strong PMOS, including input slew): t_r ≈ 0.15 ns.
- fosc ≈ 1/(3*(t_f + t_r)) = 1/(3*0.65 ns) ≈ 5.2e8 Hz.

**Step 3: Kvco and pushing**
- At Vctrl = 2.254 V the series Mn/Ms current rises from about 1.59 mA to about 1.92 mA, an increase of about 21%.
- The fall delay scales as 1/I, so fosc rises by about 16%: df ≈ 0.16*5.2e8 ≈ 8.3e7 Hz for 0.2 V.
- kvco = 8.3e7/0.2 ≈ 4.2e8 Hz/V.
- At Vdd = 3.5 V the Ms current rises only about 2.5% (through Mn gate drive and lambda).
- The voltage swing grows by about 6–8%, so fosc drops by about 2–3%, roughly 1.3e7 Hz.
- pushing = 1.3e7/0.2 ≈ 6e7 Hz/V.

**Step 4: power**
- Switching charge: 3 nodes * 0.5 pF * 3.3 V ≈ 4.95 pC per cycle.
- Short-circuit charge: about 1.2 pC per cycle, because the weak NMOS stack conducts while the strong PMOS is on.
- Iavg ≈ 6.1 pC * 5.2e8 Hz ≈ 3.1 mA.
- power_w = 3.3 V * 3.0 mA ≈ 9.5e-3 W.

baseline_results.claude_answer:
**Key assumption:** this is a 3-stage current-starved ring. The starving NMOS (Ms) sets a nearly constant pull-down current, the PMOS pull-up is much stronger, and the delay is dominated by the pull-down slewing the node load.

**1) Starving current and load**
- Ms: W/L = 7.783u/0.5343u = 14.57, so beta = 110u*14.57 = 1.60 mA/V^2.
- Ms: Vov = 1.4125 - 0.7 = 0.7125 V, so Id = 0.5*1.60m*0.7125^2*(1 + 0.04*~2.5) = 0.4066 mA*1.1 ≈ 0.45 mA.
- Mn is far stronger (W/L = 80.9, beta ≈ 8.9 mA/V^2), so it sits in deep triode with about 20 mV across it, and Ms is the current limiter.
- Cox = 3.45e-11/20n = 1.73 mF/m^2, so the next-stage gate and overlap capacitance adds about 70 fF to the 206 fF explicit cap.
- Ctot ≈ 206f + 70f ≈ 275 fF per node.

**2) Frequency**
- The PMOS (beta = 1.12 mA/V^2) trips the next stage when 0.5*1.12m*(3.3 - Vin - 0.7)^2 = 0.45 mA, which gives Vin ≈ 1.75 V.
- Pull-down delay: t_pHL ≈ Ctot*ΔV/I = 275f*(3.3 - 1.75)/0.45m ≈ 0.95 ns.
- Pull-up delay: the strong PMOS gives t_pLH ≈ 0.4 ns.
- T = 3*(t_pHL + t_pLH) ≈ 3*1.35 ns ≈ 4.0 ns, so fosc ≈ 2.5e8 Hz.

**3) Kvco and pushing**
- With Vdelta = +0.2 V, Vov goes from 0.7125 V to 0.9125 V, so I rises by (0.9125/0.7125)^2 ≈ 1.64 (to ≈ 0.73 mA).
- The PMOS trip point falls to about 1.46 V, so the discharge swing grows to 1.84 V and the discharge becomes ≈ 275f*1.84/0.73m ≈ 0.69 ns.
- Pull-up shortens to ≈ 0.35 ns, so T ≈ 3*1.04 ns ≈ 3.1 ns and f1 ≈ 3.2e8 Hz.
- kvco = (f1 - f0)/0.2 ≈ (3.2e8 - 2.5e8)/0.2 ≈ 4.5e8 Hz/V.
- Raising Vdd by 0.2 V shifts the PMOS trip point up by almost the same amount, so the discharge swing stays about 1.54 V.
- The remaining effect is channel-length modulation: Ms current rises by about 1% (0.04*0.2/1.1), giving Δf ≈ 0.01*2.5e8 ≈ 2.6e6 Hz.
- pushing ≈ 2.6e6/0.2 ≈ 1.3e7 Hz/V.

**4) Power**
- Charging current drawn from Vdd: 3 nodes * Ctot*Vdd*f = 3*275f*3.3*2.5e8 ≈ 0.68 mA.
- Short-circuit current through Ms while the PMOS pulls up: about 0.2 mA.
- Idd ≈ 0.88 mA, so pwr = 3.3*0.88 mA ≈ 2.9 mW.

baseline_results.claude_answer:
Key assumption: the ring is current-starved. The NMOS tail Ms sets the discharge current, the wide PMOS charges each node quickly, and the period is about 3 × (slow fall time + short rise time).

**Step 1 – Drive currents and loading**
- Ms: Vov = 1.7766 - 0.7 = 1.0766 V, W/L = 3.666/3.612 = 1.015, so Id = 0.5*110u*1.015*1.0766^2*(1+0.04*2.5) ≈ 71 uA. Mn is wide (W/L = 6.36) and sits in deep triode, so Ms limits the pull-down.
- Mp: Id,sat = 0.5*50u*3.586*2.6^2 ≈ 606 uA, so it is about 8x stronger than Ms.
- Load per node: C = 85.5 fF + next-stage Mn gate channel (Cox = 3.45e-11/20e-9 = 1.73 mF/m^2, so 1.73m*22.96u*3.61u = 143 fF) + overlaps and Mp gate (~28 fF) + own drain overlap (~14 fF) ≈ 270 fF. I assumed no junction caps, since AD/PD are not given.

**Step 2 – fosc**
- Discharge slope = I/C = 71 uA/270 fF ≈ 0.26 V/ns.
- The inverter trip point is where Mp's Vsg gives about 65-70 uA: Vsg ≈ 0.7 + sqrt(2*67u/(50u*3.586)) ≈ 1.55 V, so Vtrip ≈ 3.3 - 1.55 ≈ 1.8 V.
- Fall time to the trip point = (3.3 - 1.8)/0.26 ≈ 5.7 ns. The fast PMOS rise plus turn-on delay adds about 0.9 ns, so one leg ≈ 6.6 ns.
- T = 3*6.6 ns ≈ 19.8 ns, so fosc ≈ 5.05e7 Hz.

**Step 3 – kvco and pushing**
- Vctrl rises by 0.2 V to 1.9766 V, so Vov = 1.2766 V and Id scales by (1.2766/1.0766)^2 ≈ 1.41, giving about 100 uA.
- The fall slope becomes 0.37 V/ns and the trip point moves to about 1.6 V, so fall time = 1.7/0.37 ≈ 4.6 ns and the leg ≈ 5.4 ns.
- f1 = 1/(3*5.4 ns) ≈ 6.17e7 Hz, so kvco = (6.17e7 - 5.05e7)/0.2 ≈ 5.6e7 Hz/V.
- For Vdd = 3.5 V, Id rises only about 1% through lambda, but the node must swing further to the trip point (3.5 - 1.55 ≈ 1.95 V, a 1.55 V swing vs 1.5 V). Fall time = 1.55/(0.263*1.01) ≈ 5.84 ns, so f2 ≈ 4.93e7 Hz.
- pushing = |4.93e7 - 5.05e7|/0.2 ≈ 6e6 Hz/V.

**Step 4 – Power**
- Dynamic power = 3 nodes * C * Vdd^2 * f = 3*270f*10.89*5.05e7 ≈ 4.4e-4 W.
- Crowbar current while Mp and Mn are both on during the slow edges is about 11 uA average, adding about 3.7e-5 W.
- power_w ≈ 4.8e-4 W.

{"fosc_hz": 5.05e7, "kvco": 5.6e7, "pushing": 6.0e6, "power_w": 4.8e-4}

baseline_results.claude_answer:
**Assumption:** a current-starved 3-stage ring where only the pull-down is starved (Ms sets the discharge current) and the PMOS pull-up is fast. The load is about 170 fF per node: 111.6 fF of C plus about 45 fF of next-stage gate capacitance plus about 15 fF of Miller and overlap. Junction capacitance is about 0 because AD and PD are not given.

**Step 1, starving current and stage delay (Vdd=3.3 V, Vctrl=1.1286 V).**
- Ms current: Iss = 0.5*110u*(12.96/1.086)*(1.1286-0.7)^2*(1+0.04*Vds) = 0.5*110u*11.93*0.1837*1.05 = 128 uA
- Next-stage PMOS takes over when 0.5*50u*(17.7/1.086)*Vov^2 = 128 uA, so Vov = 0.56 V and the trip point is n = 3.3-0.7-0.56 = 2.05 V.
- Starved fall time: Tf = C*(3.3-2.05)/Iss = 170f*1.25/128u = 1.7 ns
- Fast Mp-driven rise to about 1.3 V, which turns on the next Mn: tr ≈ 0.9 ns
- Stage delay D = Tf + tr ≈ 2.6 ns, so T = 3*D ≈ 7.7 ns and fosc ≈ 1.3e8 Hz

**Step 2, tuning gain (Vctrl+0.2 V = 1.3286 V).**
- Iss = 0.5*110u*11.93*(0.6286)^2*1.05 = 272 uA, which is 2.1x the nominal current.
- Trip point: Vov = sqrt(2*272u/815u) = 0.82 V, so n = 3.3-0.7-0.82 = 1.78 V.
- Tf = 170f*1.52/272u = 0.95 ns and tr ≈ 0.55 ns, so D = 1.5 ns, T = 4.5 ns and f1 ≈ 2.2e8 Hz.
- kvco = (f1-f0)/0.2 = (2.2e8-1.3e8)/0.2 ≈ 4.6e8 Hz/V

**Step 3, supply pushing (Vdd 3.3 → 3.5 V).**
- The falling distance Vdd-Vtrip = 0.7+Vov_p does not depend on Vdd, and the rise timing is unchanged, so to first order the frequency is supply-independent.
- The only real dependence is channel-length modulation of Ms. Vs rises by about 0.18 V, so Iss increases by 0.04*0.18/1.065 ≈ 0.7%, which gives delta_f ≈ 0.6 MHz over 0.2 V.
- pushing ≈ 3-4e6 Hz/V

**Step 4, power.**
- Average Vdd current equals the sum of the average Ms currents, since the node-to-ground caps carry no net DC current.
- Per stage per cycle: charge ≈ C*dV + crowbar = 170f*2.9 V + about 0.2 pC ≈ 0.7 pC
- I_avg = 3*0.7 pC*1.3e8 = 0.27 mA
- power = 3.3*0.27 mA ≈ 9e-4 W

{"fosc_hz": 1.3e8, "kvco": 4.6e8, "pushing": 4.0e6, "power_w": 9.0e-4}

Vclk clk 0 PULSE(0 3.3 0 1n 1n 30n 100n)

M2 op  inn tail 0 NMOS W=1.023324e-04 L=1.615933e-06

* --- ideal 1-bit dac closing the loop back onto the summing input ---
Efb inn 0 VALUE={1.2 + 3.467555e-01*v(qh)}

* --- fixed measurement filter: three rc sections at ~159 kHz. this is the
*     decimation filter of the measurement, not part of the design ---

Cf1 f1 0 1n
Rf2 f1 f2 1k
Cf2 f2 0 1n
Rf3 f2 f3 1k

Hand analysis only; nothing was simulated, and the SNDR step below is a rough estimate that does not clearly reach 51 dB.

Step 1 (power). Ibs mirrors into M5 and the tail current flows through M3/M4, so the supply carries about 2*Ib. Pwr = 3.3*2*Ib = 3.3*2*65e-6 = 4.29e-4 W, which is under the 5.392e-4 W limit (Ib max is about 81.7 uA). Note Ib sets the tail current because M5 and M6 are both 40u/1u (1:1 mirror).

Step 2 (input pair and integrator gain). Each branch carries 32.5 uA, so with W1/L1 = 50u/1u, gm = sqrt(2*110e-6*50*32.5e-6) = 5.98e-4 S, and Vov = sqrt(2*32.5e-6/(110e-6*50)) = 0.109 V. The mirror (M3/M4, 1:1) turns the differential current into a single-ended current onto Cint. The pair saturates for |vd| > sqrt(2)*Vov = 0.154 V, so the maximum current step is about Ib = 65 uA. With Ts = 100 ns and Ci = 50 pF, the maximum voltage step is Ib*Ts/Ci = 65e-6*100e-9/50e-12 = 0.13 V per clock. That is small enough to keep op between the rails around the 1.65 V comparator threshold. It is also a large enough step for the loop to track the input. The finite DC gain gm/(gds2+gds4) ≈ 6e-4/(0.04*32.5e-6 + 0.05*32.5e-6) ≈ 200 is enough that leakage is a small effect for Ci = 50 pF.

Step 3 (feedback range and in-band noise). The loop balances when the average of Vref*q equals the input, so stability needs Ain/Vref < 1. I take Ain/Vref = 0.15/0.25 = 0.6, a large signal that still leaves headroom. For a first-order 1-bit loop at fs = 10 MHz, the normalized noise PSD is (1/3)/5e6 = 6.7e-8 /Hz, shaped by (2*pi*f/fs)^2. Integrated to 125 kHz this gives about 1.7e-5, compared with a signal power of 0.5*0.6^2 = 0.18. The ratio is about 1.06e4, or 40 dB, before the filter effects; the filter attenuates noise and signal differently, which I did not work out. This shows that SNDR rises with Ain/Vref and with a large Ci/small-step design. The 51 dB spec is not clearly met by this estimate, but this is the sizing that maximizes SNDR within the power limit.

Step 4 (resulting metrics). Power is 0.43 mW, within the 0.539 mW limit. The SNDR estimate above is the weak point, since the 50.99 dB / 8.178 ENOB targets sit above what the idealized estimate gives.

baseline_results.claude_answer:
Key assumption: the OTA drives the integrator as a nearly linear gm stage, so a 1-bit loop with the feedback ladder gives a first-order DSM whose output bit density follows Ain/Vref.

Step 1 (power): the tail current mirrors Ib (M5/M6 are both 40u/1u), and M3/M4 carry the tail current from Vdd. M5 Vds is about 0.26 V against M6 at about 0.82 V, so lambda=0.04 gives Itail = Ib*(1+0.04*0.26)/(1+0.04*0.82) = 0.978*Ib. With Ib = 35 uA, Itail = 34.2 uA and Idd = 35 uA + 34.2 uA = 69.2 uA. Power = 3.3 V * 69.2 uA = 228 uW, which is below 247.6 uW. This is about 8% margin. Ib can be at most 37.5 uA.

Step 2 (OTA linearity and gain): choose W1/L1 = 10u/3u = 3.33 so Vov is large and gm is low. Vov = sqrt(2*17 uA/(110 uA/V^2*3.33)) = 0.305 V. gm = 2*17 uA/0.305 V = 1.1e-4 S. The pair stays reasonably linear up to about sqrt(2)*Vov = 0.43 V. Ro = 1/((0.04+0.05)*17 uA) = 654 kohm, so the OTA DC gain is gm*Ro = 1.1e-4*6.5e5 = 72 (37 dB), which is enough for OSR = 10 MHz/(2*125 kHz) = 40. Choose Ci = 20 pF. Leak per clock = T/(Ro*Ci) = 100n/(654k*20p) = 0.8%. Per-cycle step = gm*0.17 V*100 ns/20 pF = 0.1 V. That is small enough that op stays around 1.65 V with M4 saturated. The 0.75 V start-up slew from about 2.4 V takes less than 1 us, well before the 9.6 us window.

Step 3 (feedback and filter): the sample switch is closed for only 30 ns of each 100 ns clock, and during hold qh is pulled to f1 through Rf1. The loop therefore sees feedback F = 0.25*q + 0.75*f1. With x = s*1us, the closed-loop transfer from input to f3 is 1/(Vref*P(x)) with P = 0.25*x^3 + 2.25*x^2 + 3.5*x + 1. At 125 kHz, x = j0.785 and |P| = 2.66, so |f3/u| = 0.377/Vref. The dominant pole is at x = -0.37 (2.7 us), so the start-up transient at 9.6 us is e^(-3.55) = 0.03 of its initial size. It contributes about 2e-5*r^2 to the variance, which is roughly 35 dB below the signal.

Step 4 (SNDR): take r = Ain/Vref = 0.45. Bit-density amplitude = r/|F| = 0.45/0.61 = 0.74, which is below 1 and leaves room for offset. With Vref = 0.2 V and Ain = 0.09 V, the OTA input offset of 5 to 18 mV adds a density offset of about 0.03 to 0.09. This is still within the loop range. Signal amplitude at f3 = 0.377*0.45 = 0.17 V, so sig^2/2 = 0.0144 V^2. The first-order shaped quantization noise after the 3-pole ladder is about 6e-6 V^2. The estimate for SNDR is 10*log10(0.0144/6e-6) = 34 dB. Allowing about 8 dB for distortion, idle tones, loop delay and leakage, SNDR is about 26 dB or better, which meets the 25.93 dB spec. ENOB is then at least (25.93 - 1.76)/6.02 = 4.02 bits. The peak differential input is 0.85*0.2 + 0.09 = 0.26 V, which stays inside the linear range from Step 2.

**Key assumption:** the bias mirror M6/M5 has equal W/L (40u/1u), so the tail current equals Ib. The 1-bit comparator and sample/hold are ideal, and the input pair works in its linear range so the modulator encodes the input instead of slewing.

**Step 1 – Power.** The supply current is the reference branch plus the tail branch, so I(Vdd) ≈ 2*Ib. With Ib = 12 uA, Ptot = 3.3 V * 2 * 12 uA = 79.2 uW, which is below 95.12 uW with about 17% margin.

**Step 2 – Input pair and linear range.**
- Each device carries Id = Ib/2 = 6 uA, and W1/L1 = 20u/2u = 10.
- Vov = sqrt(2*Id/(KP*W/L)) = sqrt(2*6e-6/(110e-6*10)) = 0.104 V, so the linear differential range is about sqrt(2)*Vov = 0.15 V.
- gm = sqrt(2*KP*(W/L)*Id) = sqrt(2*110e-6*10*6e-6) = 1.15e-4 S.
- The largest differential error is Ain + Vref = 0.065 V + 0.1 V = 0.165 V, which is only just beyond the 0.15 V linear range, so mild compression is expected near the peaks.
- The common-mode level of 1.2 V keeps the tail node at about 0.2 to 0.3 V, above M5's Vov of about 0.07 V.

**Step 3 – Loop gain and integrator swing.**
- The integrator unity-gain frequency is gm/Ci = 1.15e-4/20p = 5.75e6 rad/s, or about 0.9 MHz.
- At 125 kHz the integrator gain is gm/(w*Ci) = 1.15e-4/(7.85e5*20e-12) ≈ 7.3, which gives enough in-band loop gain for first-order shaping.
- The op swing per clock step is gm*e*T/Ci = 1.15e-4*0.1*100n/20p ≈ 58 mV, which fits well within the output range of M4 and M2.

**Step 4 – SNDR estimate.**
- The 3-pole RC at 1 us has a corner of 159 kHz and attenuates the 125 kHz tone by 0.787^3 = 0.487.
- The modulation depth is a = Ain/Vref = 0.065/0.1 = 0.65.
- The signal power is (0.487*0.65)^2/2 = 0.050 (in units of the feedback level squared).
- The ±1 quantizer has error variance 1/3. First-order shaping and the filter give an integrated noise power of (1/3)*(2/fs)*(2*pi/fs)^2*fc^3*pi/16 ≈ 2.1e-5.
- The estimated SNDR is 10*log10(0.050/2.1e-5) ≈ 33.8 dB, which gives an ENOB of (33.8 - 1.76)/6.02 ≈ 5.3 bits.
- Both figures clear the 32.19 dB and 5.056 bit targets, though only by about 1.6 dB and 0.3 bit.
- This is a white-noise estimate, so it is optimistic. It ignores idle tones, the lag from the filter loading on qh, and offset from the M3/M4 Vds mismatch (about 2 mV, small next to 100 mV).

baseline_results.claude_answer:
**Key assumption:** the SC loop behaves as a first-order modulator, with the OTA acting as a gm-C integrator that is not slew-limited. The OSR is 10 MHz / (2*125 kHz) = 40, so the ideal first-order SQNR is about 6.02*N + 1.76 - 5.17 + 30*log10(40) = 6.02*N + 44.7 dB at the modulator output. The 3-pole RC filter and the finite-OTA-gain leakage cost some of that, but with margin the targets of about 35.5 dB and 5.6 bits are reachable.

**Step 1 - Power:** the tail mirror is M5/M6 at W/L = 40u/1u, matching the reference, so Itail = Ib = 100 uA. The supply current is the bias branch plus the tail, 2*Ib = 200 uA. Power = 3.3 V * 200 uA = 0.66 mW, which is below the 1.086 mW limit.

**Step 2 - OTA transconductance and linearity:** with W1 = 20 um and L1 = 2 um, each side carries Id = 50 uA. Then gm = sqrt(2*KP*(W/L)*Id) = sqrt(2*110u*10*50u) = 0.33 mS. The overdrive is Vov = 2*Id/gm = 100u/0.33m = 0.30 V, so the differential linear range is about sqrt(2)*Vov = 0.42 V.

**Step 3 - Slew and integrator step:** the feedback is Vref = 0.2 V and the signal amplitude is Ain = 0.14 V, which is 0.7 of full scale and within the stable range. The peak OTA current is gm*(Vref + Ain) = 0.33m*0.34 = 112 uA, so it only briefly approaches the 100 uA tail limit. The feedback-dominated step is dV = gm*Vref*Ts/Ci = 0.33m*0.2*100n/20p = 0.33 V per clock. That keeps op swinging around the 1.65 V comparator threshold without hitting the rails.

**Step 4 - Leakage and SNDR:** ro is about 1/(lambda*Id) = 1/(0.045*50u) = 444 kohm, so gds is about 4.5 uS. Roughly, the pole is gds/Ci = 4.5u/20p = 2.2e5 rad/s, so the integrator leaks with tau = Ci/gds = 4.4 us, which is much longer than the 100 ns clock period. The DC gain is gm/gds, about 73 (37 dB), enough for first-order noise shaping. The signal in the output is then about 2*sqrt(yc1^2 + ys1^2), and the expected SNDR is about 38-40 dB, which gives ENOB of about 6.0-6.4 bits and clears 35.51 dB and 5.606 bits.

**Key assumption:** the OTA is a differential pair with the tail set by the 40u/1u mirror, so Itail = Ib and the supply carries 2*Ib in total (reference branch plus tail). The 1-bit loop works only while the OTA stays near its linear range, because a saturated OTA would lose the input signal.

**Step 1 (power):** P = 3.3 V * 2 * Ib = 6.6 V * 100 uA = 0.66 mW, below the 0.8624 mW limit (this allows Ib up to about 130 uA). Clock and switch currents are negligible. Ib = 100 uA.

**Step 2 (OTA linear range and bias):** Each side carries 50 uA. With W1/L1 = 40u/1u: Vov1 = sqrt(2*50u/(110u*40)) = 0.151 V, and gm1 = 2*50u/0.151 = 660 uS. The linear input range is about sqrt(2)*Vov1 = 0.21 V. Vt1 with body effect is about 0.745 V, so Vtail = 1.2 - 0.745 - 0.151 = 0.30 V. M5 needs Vov5 = sqrt(2*100u/(110u*40)) = 0.21 V, so it stays in saturation (0.30 V > 0.21 V). Mirror offset from lambda is about 1 uA / 660 uS = 1.5 mV, which the loop absorbs into the DC term ydc.

**Step 3 (feedback and signal levels):** The OTA input is Vin - Vref*bit, so Vref must be of the order of the linear range. Vref = 0.12 V gives a worst-case input difference of Ain + Vref = 0.075 + 0.12 = 0.195 V, which is inside the 0.21 V linear range. The ratio Ain/Vref = 0.625. The sampling rate is 10 MHz and the band is 125 kHz, so OSR = 40.

**Step 4 (integrator and SNDR):** Choose Ci = 100 pF. The worst-case integrator step per clock is Imax*Ts/Ci = 100u*100n/100p = 0.1 V, and the typical step is gm*Vref*Ts/Ci = 660u*0.12*100n/100p = 0.08 V. This is small against the available swing around the 1.65 V threshold, and the loop settles in a few clocks, well before 9.6 us. The DC gain is about gm*(ro1||ro3) = 660u*220k, roughly 145 (about 43 dB). The leak pole is at 1/(2*pi*22 us), about 7 kHz, which is negligible at 125 kHz. The ideal first-order SQNR is 6.02 + 1.76 - 5.17 + 30*log10(40) + 20*log10(0.625) = 50.7 - 4.1 = 46.6 dB. The 3-pole RC filter (1k/1n each) and the short 16 us window cost several dB. I expect an SNDR of about 38–40 dB, above 33.89 dB, giving ENOB = (38 - 1.76)/6.02 = 6.0 bits, above 5.333 bits.

**Step 1: power and bias.** M6 and M5 are identical (W/L = 40), so Itail ≈ Ib. M5 sees Vds ≈ 0.35 V and M6 sees Vgs ≈ 0.85 V, so Itail = 50u*(1+0.04*0.35)/(1+0.04*0.85) ≈ 49 uA. The supply current is Ib + Itail ≈ 99 uA. The clocked switch and the Bq source draw nothing from Vdd. Power = 3.3 V*99 uA ≈ 0.33 mW, which is below the 0.4503 mW limit with about 27% margin.

**Step 2: integrator gm, gain and leakage.** I assume the diode-loaded pair plus mirror acts as a gm-C integrator, with each branch carrying Itail/2 ≈ 25 uA.
- Choose W1/L1 = 100u/1u = 100.
- gm = sqrt(2*KP*(W/L)*Id) = sqrt(2*110u*100*25u) = 742 uS, with Vov = 2*25u/742u ≈ 0.07 V, so M1 and M2 stay in strong inversion.
- ro2 = 1/(0.04*25u) = 1.0 Mohm and ro4 = 1/(0.05*25u) = 0.8 Mohm, so Ro ≈ 0.44 Mohm and the DC gain is gm*Ro ≈ 330 (50 dB).
- Pick Ci = 15 pF. The leakage pole is 1/(2*pi*0.44M*15p) ≈ 24 kHz, which is below the 125 kHz tone.
- Gain at the tone is gm/(2*pi*125k*Ci) = 742u/(7.85e5*15p) ≈ 63, so the loop gain in band is high and the quantization noise is strongly suppressed.

**Step 3: slew, saturation and sliding behaviour.**
- The maximum steered current is Itail ≈ 49 uA, so the slew rate is 49u/15p ≈ 3.3 V/us. That is about 0.1 V per 30 ns clock-high window, which keeps op inside its range and crossing the 1.65 V comparator threshold.
- The diode-load DC level is about 2.4 V (Vsg ≈ 0.93 V). The lambda mismatch at op = 1.65 V leaves about 0.9 uA of systematic imbalance, which is an input-referred offset of about 0.9u/742u ≈ 1.2 mV. That is under 0.5% of Vref and is removed by the ydc subtraction.
- The comparator loop has almost no delay and the sample cap is only 0.1 pF. The loop therefore behaves as an almost sliding-mode 1-bit loop, and the filtered feedback follows vin/Vref.
- The 3-stage RC filter (1k and 1n per stage, f3dB roughly 160 kHz per isolated stage) attenuates the tone, but the in-phase and quadrature projection measurement handles the phase shift.

**Step 4: Vref and Ain for SNDR.**
- For a 1-bit loop to track, Ain must stay below Vref. I take Ain/Vref ≈ 0.67, which is near the best SNDR before overload.
- Vref = 0.3 V and Ain = 0.2 V, so the differential error stays small and the pair stays linear (Vref + Ain = 0.5 V).
- Signal in v(f3) ≈ (Ain/Vref)*0.49 ≈ 0.33 in unit-feedback terms, so sig^2/2 ≈ 0.054.
- Noise is the filtered, first-order-shaped quantization residue, strongly reduced by the loop gain of about 63. My analytical estimate of the in-band noise is about 3e-4, giving SNDR ≈ 10*log10(0.054/3e-4) ≈ 52 dB and ENOB ≈ (52 - 1.76)/6.02 ≈ 8.3 bits. This is a rough estimate and has not been checked by simulation. It would clear the specs of 48.44 dB and 7.754 bits.

baseline_results.claude_answer:
Key assumption: the loop is a first-order delta-sigma modulator, with the OTA-C integrator as the loop filter. The 1-bit quantizer is sampled at 10 MHz, and a 3-pole RC filter (about 1 kohm and 1 nF per stage) extracts the output. SNDR is computed from the filtered output over the 9.6 us to 25.6 us window, which is only 2 signal periods (8 us each).

Step 1: Power
Bias branch: Ibs = 101.8 uA, mirrored through M6 into M5 (both 40u/1u), so the tail current is about 101.8 uA.
Supply current is about 101.8 uA (tail) + 101.8 uA (bias) = 203.6 uA.
power_w = 3.3 V * 203.6 uA = 6.72e-4 W.
The ideal switch and the Efb source draw no supply current, so the total is about 0.67 mW.

Step 2: Integrator and loop behaviour
Each input transistor carries 50.9 uA, so gm = sqrt(2*KP*(W/L)*ID) = sqrt(2*110u*128*50.9u) = sqrt(1.43e-6) = 1.2 mS.
The output is single-ended at op, with a diode load (gm3 about 0.3 mS) in parallel, so the integrator is leaky.
Effective output resistance is about 1/gm4 = 3.3 kohm, giving a DC gain of about 1.2/0.3 = 4 and a pole at 1/(2*pi*3.3k*26 pF) = 1.85 MHz. This is a lossy integrator.
Differential gain from the op node is about gm1*Rload, with the load diode-connected at M3 only, which is an unbalanced mirror. The integrating action is weak, so the noise shaping is poor.

Step 3: Resolution
The feedback is 1.2 + 0.372*v(qh), where qh is the 1-bit sampled value, so the feedback is 0.828 V or 1.572 V. The input amplitude is 0.232 V, giving a ratio of 0.232/0.372 = 0.62 of full scale.
The sampled quantizer is sampled at 10 MHz with OSR = 40 for 125 kHz. An ideal first-order loop would give about 9 bits (SNDR about 55 dB), but the leaky integrator with a gain of only about 4 degrades this considerably.
The filter has a corner near 160 kHz per stage, so it passes both the signal and some of the out-of-band noise. The short 2-period window also adds error.
I estimate SNDR of about 30 dB.
enob = (30 - 1.76)/6.02 = 4.7 bits.

baseline_results.claude_answer:
Step 1 (power): The bias current is Ibs = 133.7 uA into the M6 diode. M5 has the same W/L as M6, so the tail current is ≈133.7 uA. Each M3/M4 branch carries about 66.9 uA. The supply current is the bias branch plus the tail, ≈133.7 + 133.7 = 267.4 uA. I assume the clocked switch, the B-source and the feedback network draw no supply current. power_w = 3.3 V * 267.4 uA ≈ 8.8e-4 W. Channel-length modulation raises the tail current slightly (Vds of M5 is above Vgs of M6), so I round up to about 8.9e-4 W.

Step 2 (loop): The modulator is a first-order loop. The integrator is a gm-C stage: gm1 = sqrt(2*KP*(W/L)*Id) = sqrt(2*110u*21*66.9u) = sqrt(3.09e-7) ≈ 556 uS. The mirror M3/M4 is a diode with a mirror output, so the differential current goes to the integrating node op. Cint = 53.7 pF, so the integrator gain per 100 ns clock period is gm*T/C = 556u*100n/53.7p ≈ 1.04. The feedback is 0.6*v(qh) around a 1.2 V common mode, which gives ±0.6 V. The input amplitude is 80.9 mV and the input frequency is 125 kHz. The sample rate is 10 MHz, so the OSR is about 40 if the band is 125 kHz. The ideal first-order SQNR is 6.02N + 1.76 − 5.17 + 30log10(OSR) = 6.02 + 1.76 − 5.17 + 48 ≈ 50.6 dB, with N = 1 bit. The signal is only 80.9 mV against a 600 mV reference, which costs 20*log10(0.0809/0.6) ≈ −17.4 dB. That gives about 33 dB before other effects.

Step 3 (measured SNDR): The measurement uses v(f3) over 16 us, which covers only 2 signal periods, and noise is measured across all frequencies (total power minus the signal). The 3-pole RC filter (1 kΩ, 1 nF each, corner ≈ 160 kHz per pole) removes much of the out-of-band quantization noise, but the sampling is coarse. Noise is therefore integrated over the full 5 MHz band, attenuated by the filter. The filter attenuates the signal slightly at 125 kHz (about 3 dB, plus phase shift, which does not matter here because the signal power is taken from the quadrature sum). Signal in the filter output ≈ 0.6*0.0809*0.55 ≈ 27 mV amplitude, so signal power ≈ 3.6e-4 V². The quantization noise, shaped and filtered, is of order 1e-5 V² or higher. baseline_results.claude_answer:
Key assumption: the modulator is a 10 MHz clocked first-order loop (100 ns period) with a 1-bit quantizer, and the OSR is large. The SNDR is estimated from the quantization-noise limit, with the filter and the loop's non-idealities as the main corrections.

Step 1 (power): The bias current is Ibs = 240.4 uA, mirrored by M6 (40u/1u) into M5 (40u/1u) at a 1:1 ratio, so the tail current is about 240 uA. The mirror branch also draws 240 uA from Vdd. The tail splits between M1/M3 and M2/M4, so the amplifier branches together draw about 240 uA. The static supply current is therefore about 240 + 240 = 480 uA. The 0.1 pF sampling-capacitor switching current is negligible. power_w = 3.3 V * 480 uA = 1.58 mW. Since the clock has a 30% duty cycle, the average of the absolute supply current stays at roughly this value.

Step 2 (loop behavior): The M1/M2 pair has W/L = 58.5. It is biased at 120 uA per side, so gm = sqrt(2 * 110u * 58.5 * 120u) = sqrt(1.545e-6) = 1.24 mS. The OTA load is a diode-connected PMOS (M3) with mirror output M4, so the output resistance is about 1/(lambda*I) ≈ 1/(0.045 * 120u) ≈ 185 kohm. The integrator then has a finite DC gain of about gm*ro ≈ 230 (47 dB), and the integrator is leaky. Cint = 74.7 pF, so the leaky pole sits at 1/(2*pi*185k*74.7p) ≈ 11.5 kHz. The ideal integrator gain per sample is gm*T/Cint = 1.24m * 100n / 74.7p ≈ 1.66 V per V. This is a very high loop gain, with a leaky pole at 11.5 kHz. The feedback is fb = 1.2 + 0.6*qh, and the sampled output swings 0.6 V ± 1 around the 1.2 V common mode.

Step 3 (SNDR): The input amplitude is 63.8 mV. The feedback step is ±0.6 V, so the full-scale input is 0.6 V and the input is at about -19.4 dB relative to full scale. The sampling clock is 10 MHz and the signal is 125 kHz, so the output filter is a 3-pole RC with fc = 1/(2*pi*1k*1n) = 159 kHz per pole. That makes the filter bandwidth about 100 kHz, which is only slightly above the 125 kHz signal frequency. The signal is attenuated and phase-shifted, and the measurement uses the cos/sin demodulation, so the phase does not matter. Noise is everything left in v(f3) after the signal is removed, which includes the filtered quantization noise. The filter passes noise with an effective bandwidth of about 160 kHz*1.5 → ~80 kHz equivalent, so the wide-band noise reaching the output is greater than that within the 125 kHz signal band alone. Noise from the first-order shaping at OSR ≈ 10M/2/160k ≈ 31 gives SQNR(max) = 6.02 + 1.76 - 5.17 + 30*log10(31) = 2.6 + 44.7 ≈ 47 dB at full scale. At -19 dB input amplitude this is reduced to about 28 dB. The leaky integrator and the idling tones add further degradation, so I estimate SNDR ≈ 26 dB.

enob = (26 - 1.76)/6.02 ≈ 4.0 bits.

baseline_results.claude_answer:
Key assumption: the loop is a 1-bit first-order modulator. The OTA-style stage integrates onto Cint, the comparator makes the decision, and the sample-and-hold output is fed back through a 3-pole RC filter. The clock is 10 MHz and the signal is at 125 kHz. Over the 16 us window that gives 2 signal cycles, and the measurement window includes only 160 clock samples.

Step 1: bias and power
- Ibs = 113.8 uA. M6 is 40u/1u and M5 is 40u/1u, so the mirror ratio is 1 and Itail = 113.8 uA.
- Supply current = Ibs + Itail = 227.6 uA.
- The tail current splits between M1/M2 and flows through the M3/M4 load, so it is already counted in Itail.
- The clock source Vclk is a separate source and does not count in i(Vdd).
- Charging of Csh = 0.1p through the 3-RC filter from the switch adds a negligible current of order 1 uA.
- Power ≈ 3.3 * 227.6u = 0.75 mW. Allowing for slight current variation, power_w ≈ 7.5e-4 W.

Step 2: loop gain and feedback
- The input differential is Vid = Vin - Vfb.
- Each side carries 57 uA, and gm of the M1/M2 pair at W/L = 35.3 and KP = 110u gives gm = sqrt(2*110u*35.3*57u) = 0.67 mS.
- The current into Cint per clock step is the differential current gm*Vid, integrated onto Cint = 15.9 pF.
- The feedback is Efb = 1.2 + 0.1231*v(qh), where qh = ±1, so the feedback step is ±0.123 V around 1.2 V.
- The input amplitude is 35.4 mV, which is 0.29 of the feedback full scale, so the modulator is stable and not overloaded.
- The integrator is not a true integrator on the input side (the load is diode-connected M3 with M4 mirroring), so the op node behaves as an integrator with Cint on the op output.
- The integrator gain per clock is gm*T/Cint = 0.67m*100n/15.9p ≈ 4.2 V/V per unit differential, which is far larger than 1. Effective loop gain per sample is therefore about 4.2*0.123 ≈ 0.5 V/V relative to the 0.123 V feedback step, so the integrator is saturating with large gain.
- The mirror is also imperfect (om is diode-connected at the 1/gm_p level while op has output resistance only), which leaves a leaky integrator with finite DC gain of order gm*ro ≈ 0.67m/(0.0045m) ≈ 100.

Step 3: SNDR
- A first-order modulator with an OSR of 10M/(2*125k) = 40 would give about 6.02*N + 1.76 - 5.17 + 30*log10(40) = 9 + 48 = 57 dB (OSR = 40).
- Here the measurement counts all noise as ytot - sig^2/2 without band-limiting, but v(f3) is filtered by the 3-pole RC filter (RC = 1 us, a corner of about 160 kHz).
- The filter attenuates the quantization noise above 160 kHz, but the signal sits at 125 kHz and is also attenuated, so the filter's inband noise is the main contribution.
- The window is short, 2 cycles, and the signal averaging leaves tone leakage and a startup transient, since the window starts at 9.6 us.
- Residual noise includes low-frequency idle-tone content, and the leaky integrator adds some error. I estimate SNDR ≈ 30 dB.
- enob = (30 - 1.76)/6.02 = 4.7 bits.

Step 4: result
- sndr_db ≈ 30, enob ≈ 4.7, power_w ≈ 7.5e-4.

Key assumption: the loop is a first-order, 1-bit delta-sigma modulator clocked at 10 MHz (100 ns period). The OTA integrates a gm-based current onto Cint, the comparator is a 1-bit quantizer, and the feedback passes through a 3-pole RC filter. The signal band is 125 kHz, the sampled output is filtered by RC poles with a 1 us time constant each, and the measurement window is 16 us (2 signal cycles).

Step 1 - Power. The bias current is Ibs = 225.6 uA, mirrored 1:1 (M5 and M6 both 40u/1u) into the tail, so the tail current is about 225.6 uA, plus the mirror branch of 225.6 uA.
Supply current = 225.6 uA + 225.6 uA = 451.2 uA, since the tail current flows through M3/M4 and the Ibs branch goes through M6. The tail current is a little higher because of lambda effects, so about 460 uA.
pwr = 3.3 V * 460 uA = 1.5e-3 W.

Step 2 - Modulator behavior. The loop is a first-order modulator with OSR = 10 MHz / (2 * 125 kHz) = 40. The integrator is nonideal: it is a gm-C stage driven from the sample-and-hold, but the quantizer decides on the sign of v(op) vs 1.65 V.
Feedback is 1.2 + 0.2678 * qh, where qh = +/-1 V, so the feedback is +/-0.268 V. The input amplitude is 0.2755 V, which exceeds the feedback level of 0.2678 V. This overloads the modulator (a ratio of 1.03), so the bit stream saturates at the peaks and distortion appears.

Step 3 - SNDR. The ideal first-order SQNR at OSR 40 is 6.02 + 1.76 - 5.17 + 30*log10(40) = 6.02 + 1.76 - 5.17 + 48.06 = about 50.7 dB. Overload at the input peaks, plus the 16 us window (just 2 cycles), the 3-pole filter that leaves out-of-band noise in the measurement (ysq counts all noise up to the filter cutoff, since the measurement is broadband), and the missing 1 V -> unit mismatch all pull this down. The broadband noise in the measurement is only partly shaped by the filter, a 3-pole RC at 159 kHz, which passes much of the noise near 125 kHz, and the amplitude overload adds harmonic error.
Estimated SNDR is about 20 dB.
enob = (20 - 1.76) / 6.02 = 3.0 bits.

baseline_results.claude_answer:
Assumptions: a 1-bit quantizer clocked at 10 MHz (100 ns period, sampled while clk is high) with a 3-stage RC filter on the feedback. The signal is 125 kHz, so the OSR is about 40 if the band is set by the 125 kHz tone, or higher if the band is defined by the measurement window. The integrator is a gm-C stage with Cint = 78.4 pF.

Step 1 – Power. The bias current is Ibs = 160.2 uA, mirrored by M5/M6 (both W/L = 40, so a 1:1 ratio). Tail current = 160.2 uA, flowing through the diff pair and the M3/M4 loads, so the supply current is about 160.2 + 160.2 = 320 uA. Power = 3.3 * 320.4 uA = 1.06 mW. The clock source and the Bq source are not on Vdd, so they add nothing.

Step 2 – Integrator gain. Each side of the pair carries 80 uA. gm of M1 = sqrt(2 * KP * (W/L) * ID) = sqrt(2 * 110u * 102.7 * 80u) = sqrt(1.808e-6) = 1.34 mS. Mirror M3/M4 is diode-connected, so the output current is roughly gm*(vin - vfb), with a tail-split differential gain. Integration gain per clock = gm * Ts / Cint = 1.34e-3 * 100n / 78.4p = 1.7 (counting the differential current through the mirror, so the effective gain is gm*vd). The integrator is lossy: the output resistance is about 1/(lambda*I) = 1/(0.045 * 80u) = 280 kohm, so DC gain = gm*Ro = 375 and the pole is at 1/(2*pi*280k*78p) = 7.3 kHz. This is a leaky integrator with a finite pole near 7 kHz. At 125 kHz the integrator gain is still about 17x, so the loop works, but noise shaping is weak.

Step 3 – SNDR. Feedback is 0.1709 * (+/-1) = +/-0.171 V and the input amplitude is 0.0598 V, so the loop is not overloaded (0.0598 < 0.171). The feedback filter adds 3 RC stages (tau = 1 us each) that delay the feedback and attenuate the quantization noise. With a leaky first-order loop the in-band noise is large. The filter at 125 kHz attenuates the signal by about 1/(1 + (2*pi*125k*1us)^2)^1.5 = 0.5, plus a large phase shift. The loop is therefore not strictly modulating a sampled signal, and quantization noise is about 3 dB per octave worse than ideal. Overall, ytot includes all noise to 5 MHz, so the "noise" is the full out-of-band 1-bit noise passing through the RC filter. The RC filter cuts that noise above about 160 kHz, but a residual remains. The noise power is roughly (0.171)^2 * (fraction passed, about 0.05) = 1.5e-3 V^2, against a signal of v(f3) amplitude about 0.171 * 0.06/0.171 * 0.5 = 0.03 V, so sig^2/2 = 4.5e-4 V^2. The estimated SNDR is about 4.5e-4 / 1.5e-3, near -5 dB, but the integrator gain is high and the loop tracks, so I expect the noise to be lower, giving an estimated SNDR of about 15 dB. The window is only 16 us (2 signal cycles), which adds more error. ENOB = (15 - 1.76)/6.02 = 2.2 bits.

baseline_results.claude_answer:
Key assumption: a 1-bit first-order modulator clocked at 10 MHz (100 ns period), with 125 kHz signal in a measurement window of 16 µs (2 signal cycles, 160 clock samples). There is no explicit oversampling-ratio band filter. The SNDR is computed from all noise in the output, taken after a 3-pole RC filter (1k/1n each, corner ~160 kHz).

Step 1: Power.
Tail current: Ibs mirrored through M6 (40u/1u) to M5 (40u/1u), so Itail ≈ 125.9 µA, ignoring the lambda mismatch.
Supply current: Ibs + Itail = 125.9 µA + 125.9 µA ≈ 251.8 µA, plus the diode-connected pair load which is already included in Itail.
Static power: 3.3 V * 251.8 µA = 0.831 mW.
The comparator, switch and feedback are ideal sources and draw no Vdd current.
power_w ≈ 8.3e-4 W.

Step 2: Signal level.
Input amplitude 0.1223 V. The feedback is 0.3488 * v(qh), with qh = ±1 sampled, so the full-scale feedback amplitude is 0.3488 V.
The loop gain scale gives the signal ratio 0.1223/0.3488 = 0.35 of full scale.
The output signal at v(f3) is amplified by 0.3488 * 0.35 ≈ 0.1223 V (the loop forces the feedback to track the input), and the 3-pole filter attenuates 125 kHz: |H| = 1/(1+(f/fc)^2)^1.5 roughly, but the RC ladder has fc about 0.1/(2π*RC) with loading, giving ~0.5 attenuation. That makes sig ≈ 0.35 * 0.3488 * 0.5 ≈ 0.06 V.

Step 3: Noise.
The first-order modulator's quantization noise in the full 5 MHz band is mostly removed by the RC filter (attenuating above ~200 kHz). The OSR is 40 for a 125 kHz signal band, so theoretical SQNR is about 6.02 + 1.76 - 5.17 + 30*log10(40) ≈ 52 dB for an ideal loop. The measurement uses total noise power through the filter (which is wider than 125 kHz), the integrator has finite gain from the 0.1 pF sampling loop (the 100 fF Csh cap holds the charge and Rleak at 100 MΩ with 10 ns steps is negligible), and the 30 ns on-time of the 100 ns clock gives a 30% sampling window. Assumptions: Level-1 square-law devices, with the M2/M3 mirror carrying essentially the Ibs reference current. M1 is the source follower, with its body tied to ground, so body effect applies. Channel-length modulation is included.

Beta3 = KP*W/L = 110u*56.636u/0.80484u = 110u*70.37 = 7.74 mA/V^2.
Vov3 = sqrt(2*Ibs/beta3/(1+lambda*Vds)), and with Vds = Vgs3 this gives roughly 0.223 V.
Vgs3 ≈ 0.923 V, so (1+0.04*0.92) = 1.037 and the mirror is nearly matched.
M2 has Vds = Vout, which is about 1.9 V at the DC point, so (1+0.04*1.9) = 1.076.
I2 ≈ 193.5u*1.076/1.037 ≈ 201 uA.
The DC output is about 1.9 V, so RL draws about 1.9/51k = 37 uA.
M1 therefore carries about 201 + 37 ≈ 238 uA.
Check on Vout: M1 beta = 110u*(103.03/2.1057) = 110u*48.93 = 5.38 mA/V^2.
Vov1 = sqrt(2*238u/5.38m/(1+0.04*1.4)) ≈ 0.29 V.
Vt with body effect, Vsb ≈ 1.1 V: Vt = 0.7 + 0.4*(sqrt(1.8) - sqrt(0.7)) = 0.7 + 0.4*(1.342 - 0.837) = 0.90 V.
Vout = 1.471 - 0.90 - 0.29 ≈ 0.28 V. This does not match the 1.9 V guess, so I iterate with the lower Vout.
At Vout ≈ 0.3 V: Vsb = 0.3 and Vt = 0.7 + 0.4*(sqrt(1.0) - 0.837) = 0.765 V.
I2 = 193.5u*(1+0.04*0.3)/1.037 ≈ 189 uA.
RL draws 0.3/51k ≈ 6 uA, so I1 ≈ 195 uA.
Vov1 ≈ sqrt(2*195u/5.38m/1.012) ≈ 0.268 V.
Vout ≈ 1.471 - 0.765 - 0.268 ≈ 0.44 V.
At Vout = 0.44 V: Vt = 0.7 + 0.4*(sqrt(1.14) - 0.837) = 0.7 + 0.4*0.231 = 0.792 V.
I2 ≈ 190 uA and the RL current is 8.6 uA, so I1 ≈ 199 uA and Vov1 ≈ 0.27 V.
Vout ≈ 1.471 - 0.792 - 0.27 ≈ 0.41 V. This converges at about 0.42 V.
iq = Vdd supply current = I1 + Ibs = 199u + 193.5u ≈ 3.93e-4 A.

Step 2 (swing): The input swings 0.771 to 2.171 V. On the negative half-cycle, Vout falls from 0.42 V while the follower gm drops.
M1 turns off when Vgs approaches Vt, around Vin ≈ 0.8 V, so Vout is pinned near 0 V by M2 and RL.
Vout is roughly 0 at the bottom, with M2 in triode and Vds → 0.
On the positive half-cycle, Vin = 2.17 V and Vout = Vin - Vt - Vov, with Vt ≈ 1.0 V (Vsb ≈ 1.1 V) at the top.
The current is mostly set by M2 (about 190 uA plus RL), and RL = 51k at Vout = 1.0 V draws only 20 uA.
Vov1 ≈ 0.3 V, Vt ≈ 0.7 + 0.4*(sqrt(1.7+...) - 0.837), roughly 0.9 V at Vout ≈ 1.0 V.
Vout_max ≈ 2.17 - 0.93 - 0.29 ≈ 0.95 V.
Swing ≈ 0.95 - 0.0 ≈ 0.95 V peak-to-peak (the bottom is clipped, with a small residual).

Step 3 (THD): The 0.7 V input amplitude causes strong clipping at the bottom, because M1 cuts off and the output is held near 0 V.
The distortion is large, with a clipped fraction of the waveform of about 30%, giving a THD of roughly 15%.

Vth = 0.7 + 0.4*(sqrt(1.136) - 0.837) = 0.7 + 0.4*0.229 = 0.792 V, Vov1 = sqrt(2*48.5u/(110u*56.25*1.04)) = 0.123 V, Vgs1 = 0.915 V, Vout = 0.485 V. baseline_results.claude_answer:
Step 1 (bias current): M3 is diode-connected and mirrors Ibs to M2. The ratio is 1:1 (same W/L), so M2 carries about Ibs = 39.15 uA, ignoring the lambda mismatch. The mirror error is small: the M3 Vds is about 0.9 V and M2 Vds is about 1.6 V, so M2 current is roughly 39.15u*(1+0.04*1.6)/(1+0.04*0.9) = 39.15u*1.064/1.036 = 40.2 uA. Output DC level: M1 must supply M2's current plus the RL current. Vout is about 1.2 V, so RL draws about 3.4 uA, giving M1 about 43.6 uA. Ibs also flows from Vdd. iq = I(M1) + Ibs = 43.6u + 39.15u = 82.8 uA.

Step 2 (swing): the input amplitude is 0.7 V, a 1.4 V pp input. The source follower gain is gm1*(ro||RL||ro2)/(1 + gm1*(...) + gmb term). gm1 = sqrt(2*KP*(W/L)*I) = sqrt(2*110u*137.7*43.6u) = sqrt(1.32e-6) = 1.15 mS. W/L1 = 1.394e-4/1.0127e-6 = 137.7. Load resistance: ro2 = 1/(0.04*40u) = 625k, ro1 = 1/(0.04*43.6u) = 573k, RL = 351k, so the parallel combination is about 1/(1.6u+1.75u+2.85u) = 161k. gm*R = 1.15m*161k = 185. gmb = gm*0.4/(2*sqrt(0.7+Vsb)), with Vsb of about 1.2 V this gives gmb/gm = 0.4/(2*1.38) = 0.145, so gmb = 0.167 mS. Gain = 185/(1+185+0.145*185) = 185/212.8 = 0.87.

Check for clipping at the extremes. Vin ranges from 1.29 V to 2.69 V. At the low end Vout is about 0.5 V. The required Vgs is about 0.7 + 0.2 = 0.9 V plus body-effect changes, which is acceptable. M2 stays saturated (Vdsat about 0.2 V), so no clipping. At the high end Vout is about 1.9 V and Vgs1 is about 0.9 V, leaving the input well within range. Swing = 1.4*0.87 = 1.22 V pp.

Step 3 (THD): nonlinearity comes from the body effect, since gm varies with Vsb and the Level-1 square law adds lambda effects. Here the gain varies with Vout because Vgs changes as sqrt(I) and Vt changes with Vsb. The Vgs overdrive is about 0.2 V with a 0.6 V swing, which implies a fairly large gain change. With a constant load current most of the Vgs variation is small, but the current into RL varies by about ±1.7 uA out of 43 uA, so Vov changes by about 2%. The dominant error is the body effect: dVt/dVout = 0.145, which varies over the swing by about 0.145*(change in gmb ratio), giving second-harmonic distortion of about 0.5% and a smaller third harmonic. The channel-length modulation of M1 adds a Vds dependence, and the swing in Vds is about ±0.6 V, adding roughly 0.3%. Estimated THD is about 0.6%.
